heard: The universe's brightest explosions were found hunting for secret nuclear bombs. In 1967, the United States launched military Vila satellites to catch banned atomic tests in space. Sensors soon detected a mysterious flash of gamma radiation that matched no known weapon signature. The discovery stayed strictly classified for six years until researchers finally published the data in 1973. These gamma-ray bursts erupt when massive stars collapse or dense neutron stars collide in deep space. A single event releases more energy in seconds than our sun will produce in its entire 10-billion-year life. Orbiting observatories now detect roughly one of these cosmic flashes every day across the universe. That is how hunting for secret nuclear bombs revealed the universe's brightest explosions.
